Definition: from G1223 and the base of G4249; to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--cut (to the heart).
BiblicalUsage: This word means to be cut to the heart, sawn asunder by anger, and the form in the text is the middle voice of the same verb. The council is cut to the heart when the apostles speak, and again when Stephen speaks, and in both places the cutting leads to rage, not repentance.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a heart can be cut in two directions; the same word that describes the council's fury describes a wound that could have led to repentance, and the tragedy is that they chose rage over the sorrow that saves.
